title: Tapping Data Acquisition & Verification
status_reason: All standards-layer claims given in the phase brief were independently verified and correctly reflected in the knowledge layer. Two design cautions from T1 (hole-preparation axis, RELATES_TO sufficiency) were resolved. However, no Tier-1 per-size numeric cross-verification of tap-drill values or thread-engagement targets against a primary standard's own table was completed in this pass — that acquisition work remains open, honestly reported as unavailable/derived_candidate rather than fabricated.

standards_verified.change: added edition/standard_status fields, noted 2013 withdrawal in public_summary
title corrected to include UNJ; scope expanded to UN/UNR/UNJ; added edition/standard_status fields

standards_still_unavailable: No standard's own published table content (drill-size tables, tolerance tables, dimension tables) was obtained in this phase — existence/status/scope only.

value_counts.note: Unchanged from T1: all 20 existing tapping_profile records' hole_preparation values remain sourced by direct reference to pre-existing verified BoltLab thread datasets. No record was newly cross-verified against an external standard's table in T2; none were altered.

thread_engagement_findings.conclusion: General engagement formula confirmed and documented as a derived_candidate on unc_tapping and unf_tapping (metric shares the same underlying relationship but the metric-specific derived_candidate added targets the ISO 2306 drill-sizing rule instead). No target_engagement_percent value was written into any record. The commonly-cited 75% UNC/UNF target was explicitly NOT promoted to verified or written into any record — it appears only as descriptive, clearly-labeled unconfirmed (Tier 3) context inside the derived_candidate.

tap_type_findings.conclusion: T1's existing definitions were checked against ASME B94.9's style list and found consistent; no definition text required correction.

hole_preparation_findings.conclusion: T1's caution resolved: the 5 entities are now explicitly documented as points along 3 distinct axes rather than one flat mutually-exclusive taxonomy. No entity definition or relationship was altered.

relationship_predicate_findings.conclusion: T2's standard-to-entity connections use each standard record's own pre-existing related_entities array (the same mechanism iso_965_1/asme_b1_1 already used), not relationships.seed.json. RELATES_TO's sufficiency for the existing 41 edges remains an open question, not required to be resolved by this phase's actual data.

source_conflicts.note: No two sources gave conflicting values for the same claim in this phase; the ASME-B94.9-attribution-of-75%-engagement claim was treated as unconfirmed (not a conflict, an unverified attribution) rather than accepted or rejected outright.
